# Lause design system

Lause is the design system behind an Estonian-citizenship exam trainer: tokens, components, and the usage rules an AI tool needs before touching this code. This file and components.manifest.json are generated by `npm run build:manifest` — read them before the source.

## Tokens

color.ground: #e3ecf7 (light) · #091727 (dark) — page background
color.ink: #0f2238 (light) · #e3ecf7 (dark) — text, filled controls
color.dim: #446081 (light) · #95b4d9 (dark) — secondary text; solid so contrast is checkable
color.accent: #d93405 (light) · #ff5a36 (dark) — graphic accent: underlines, current segment, lit edge
color.accent-text: #a92400 (light) · #ffb19e (dark) — accent used as small text
color.accent-on-ink: #ff5a36 (light) · #d93405 (dark) — accent on ink fills; full-strength coral reads on navy
color.accent-text-on-ink: #ff5a36 (light) · #a92400 (dark) — accent used as small text on ink fills
color.surface: #ffffff (light) · #0f2238 (dark) — tiles
color.on-ink: #e3ecf7 (light) · #091727 (dark) — text on ink fills
color.ink-hover: #2d4460 (light) · #cddcf0 (dark) — hover on ink fills
color.ink-active: #091727 (light) · #b2cae7 (dark) — pressed on ink fills
color.ground-hover: #cddcf0 (light) · #0f2238 (dark) — hover fill on ground-level controls
color.surface-hover: #f0f6fc (light) · #2d4460 (dark) — hover fill on tiles
font.content: Young Serif, Georgia, serif (light) · Young Serif, Georgia, serif (dark)
font.chrome: Instrument Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif (light) · Instrument Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif (dark)
type.label: fontFamily Instrument Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif, fontSize 13px, lineHeight 1.3, fontWeight 600 (light) · fontFamily Instrument Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif, fontSize 13px, lineHeight 1.3, fontWeight 600 (dark)
type.body: fontFamily Instrument Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif, fontSize 16px, lineHeight 1.5, fontWeight 400 (light) · fontFamily Instrument Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif, fontSize 16px, lineHeight 1.5, fontWeight 400 (dark)
type.title: fontFamily Instrument Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif, fontSize 19px, lineHeight 1.3, fontWeight 600 (light) · fontFamily Instrument Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif, fontSize 19px, lineHeight 1.3, fontWeight 600 (dark)
type.reading: fontFamily Young Serif, Georgia, serif, fontSize 57px, lineHeight 1.85, fontWeight 400 (light) · fontFamily Young Serif, Georgia, serif, fontSize 57px, lineHeight 1.85, fontWeight 400 (dark)
type.headline: fontFamily Young Serif, Georgia, serif, fontSize 83px, lineHeight 1.1, fontWeight 400 (light) · fontFamily Young Serif, Georgia, serif, fontSize 83px, lineHeight 1.1, fontWeight 400 (dark)
type.display: fontFamily Young Serif, Georgia, serif, fontSize 143px, lineHeight 1.1, fontWeight 400 (light) · fontFamily Young Serif, Georgia, serif, fontSize 143px, lineHeight 1.1, fontWeight 400 (dark)
radius.control: 999px (light) · 999px (dark)
radius.card: 22px (light) · 22px (dark)
radius.bubble: 10px (light) · 10px (dark)
radius.keycap: 4px (light) · 4px (dark) — keyboard hints
shadow.tile: color rgba(15, 34, 56, 0.10), offsetX 0px, offsetY 6px, blur 18px, spread 0px (light) · color rgba(15, 34, 56, 0.10), offsetX 0px, offsetY 6px, blur 18px, spread 0px (dark)

## Components

## Keycap

A keyboard hint. Inherits its colour, so it follows the text of whatever holds it.

### Props
- held?: boolean = false — Drawn filled while the key is physically held, as ⌥ is during a peek.

States: Default, Held, Row, Dark

Source: packages/ui/src/Keycap/Keycap.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (set 8:9)

## Button

A pill button. Every control in Lause shows its key, so pass `keycap` whenever there is one.

### Props
- variant?: 'filled' | 'outline' | 'dim' = 'filled' — filled: the one primary action. outline: secondary. dim: tertiary, text only.
- keycap?: string — The key that triggers this action; drawn as a Keycap after the label.

States: Filled, Hover, DisabledNoHover, Outline, Dim, Disabled, Bar, Dark

### Rules
- Every control shows its key: pass keycap whenever there is one.
- filled is the one primary action on a screen.
- Disabled controls never hover.

Source: packages/ui/src/Button/Button.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (set 9:65)

## Progress

The segmented bar under every screen: done in ink, current in accent, the rest faint.

### Props
- total: number — Number of units: sentences, cards, questions, arrows.
- current: number — Zero-based index of the current unit. Units before it are done. Pass `total` when everything is done.
- label: string — Accessible name, e.g. "Lause 5 / 8".

States: Midway, First, Last, Complete, Exam, Dark

### Rules
- One segment per unit; the counts are given in words.

Source: packages/ui/src/Progress/Progress.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (component 9:69)

## Bar

Coverage of one domain: one segment per article. Read and retained in ink, read but not retained in accent, unread faint.

### Props
- segments: readonly BarSegment[] — One entry per article, in article order.
- label: string — The counts in words, e.g. "Riigikord: 4 kinnistunud, 2 loetud, 4 lugemata, kokku 10". This is the accessible name.

States: Domain, Untouched, Rows, Dark

### Rules
- One segment per unit; the counts are given in words.

Source: packages/ui/src/Bar/Bar.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (component 9:81)

## Dial

A segmented control that behaves as a radio group: arrow keys move and select, Home/End jump.

### Props
- options: readonly DialOption<V>[] — Two or three positions.
- value: V
- onChange: (value: V) => void
- label: string — Accessible name of the group, e.g. "Tugi".
- disabled?: boolean = false

States: Support, Hover, Keyboard, TwoPositions, Disabled, Dark

### Rules
- The exam disables it as one control.

Source: packages/ui/src/Dial/Dial.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (set 10:35)

## Tile

An option or word tile. Tiles stack vertically in a TileStack; they never sit in a row except the two of a true/false item.

### Props
- state?: 'idle' | 'selected' | 'filled' | 'dimmed' = 'idle' — idle: available. selected: chosen, accent ring. filled: written in, ink. dimmed: no longer relevant.
- keycap?: string — The number key that picks this tile.

States: Idle, Selected, Hover, Filled, Dimmed, Stack, TrueFalse, Dark

### Rules
- Options stack vertically in a TileStack, never in a row, except the two of a true/false item.
- Options run to 40 characters.

Source: packages/ui/src/Tile/Tile.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (set 11:69)

## TileStack

The column that holds option tiles: 640px wide at most, one tile per row.

### Props
- label: string — Accessible name of the group, e.g. "Vali õige vastus".

States: Idle, Selected, Hover, Filled, Dimmed, Stack, TrueFalse, Dark

Source: packages/ui/src/Tile/Tile.tsx

## Bubble

A translation bubble that sits above the word it belongs to. Render it inside an element with
`position: relative`; it centres itself over that element and draws a tail down to it.

### Props
- children: ReactNode — The translation.
- count?: number — How many times this term has been looked up; shown as ×N in accent.
- note?: string — A short note after the count, e.g. the app's promotion text.

States: Pinned, Promoted, NoCount, Dark

### Rules
- Sits above its word; the count is decorative to assistive technology.

Source: packages/ui/src/Bubble/Bubble.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (component 12:5)

## Sentence

The reading unit: one sentence at reading size, its neighbours dimmed, its terms openable.

### Props
- segments: readonly Segment[] — The sentence in reading order: plain strings and markable terms.
- previous?: string — The neighbours, dimmed above and below.
- next?: string
- support: 'et' | 'tugi' | 'korvuti' — The dial level. et: no marks, terms still open. tugi: marks. korvuti: marks and the English under.
- pinned: readonly string[] — Term ids whose bubble is shown.
- counts?: Readonly<Record<string, number>> = {} — Look-up tally per term id, shown in the bubble.
- notes?: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {} — Per-term note shown after the count, e.g. the promotion text at three look-ups.
- peeking?: boolean = false — While true every gloss shows, pinned or not.
Announces nothing; the glosses are already in the accessibility tree and the app decides whether to announce the mode.
- english?: { text: string; note: string } — The Riigi Teataja English and the fixed unofficial-translation line, shown under the sentence
in korvuti; the note is never optional because the text is an unofficial translation of
constitutional law.
- onToggle: (termId: string) => void — Called with the term id when a term is clicked or opened with Enter/Space.
- label: string — Accessible name of the reading region, e.g. "Lause 5 / 8".

States: Tugi, Keyboard, TwoPins, Peeking, EestiKeeles, Korvuti, RepeatedTerm, Narrow, Dark

### Rules
- The English pair (text + note) is required together: the note says the translation is unofficial.
- Term ids that repeat pin together.

Source: packages/ui/src/Sentence/Sentence.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (set 14:322)

## usePeek

The peek gesture: hold the modifier and every translation shows; release and it goes.
A latch holds the same state without the key. The held modifier clears when the window
loses focus or is hidden; the latch is the app's and survives blur. The modifier's keydown
is cancelled so it cannot move focus to the browser's menu bar.

### Props
- latched?: boolean = false — The latch: holds the peek on without the key.
- key?: string = 'Alt' — The modifier that peeks while held.
- enabled?: boolean = true — Set false to register no listeners and report `held: false`, e.g. while the reader is off-screen.

Source: packages/ui/src/usePeek/usePeek.ts

## Nav

The top chrome: context left, caps navigation centre, controls right.

### Props
- context: ReactNode — Top-left: where the learner is, e.g. "§ 60 · lause 5 / 8".
- items: readonly NavItem[] — The centre items. Empty in exam mode.
- current?: string — The current item's id.
- peeking?: boolean = false — While true the items read their English labels. The chrome swaps; it never gains a subtitle.
- controls?: ReactNode — Top-right: the dial and the peek hint, or the exam's one action.
- label: string — Accessible name of the navigation.
- onNavigate?: (id: string) => void — Supply this when the app owns routing. A plain left-click then calls it with the item id and
suppresses the browser's own navigation; modifier and middle clicks still open the link.
Leave it out and the links navigate by themselves.

States: Reader, Peeking, Exam, Dark

### Rules
- Chrome stays Estonian; while peeking it swaps to English and never gains a subtitle.

Source: packages/ui/src/Nav/Nav.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (set 15:71)

## Cell

One cell of the 2×2 drill: the subject, the verdict, and its key.

### Props
- subject: string — The row's subject, e.g. "Igaüks".
- verdict?: string — The column's verdict, e.g. "tohib piirata".
- keycap?: string — The number key that picks this cell.
- state?: 'idle' | 'selected' | 'filled' | 'dimmed' = 'idle'

States: Idle, Selected, Filled, Dimmed, Grid, Dark

### Rules
- Rows Igaüks / Eesti kodanik, columns Tohib piirata / Ei tohi piirata; keys 1–4.

Source: packages/ui/src/Cell/Cell.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (set 16:101)

## CellGrid

The 2×2 drill laid out as a table, so the headers are read with each cell.

### Props
- rows: readonly [string, string] — The two row headers, top to bottom.
- columns: readonly [string, string] — The two column headers, left to right.
- label: string — Accessible name of the table.
- children: readonly [ReactNode, ReactNode, ReactNode, ReactNode] — Exactly four cells, in reading order: row 1 left, row 1 right, row 2 left, row 2 right.
- className?: string

States: Idle, Selected, Filled, Dimmed, Grid, Dark

Source: packages/ui/src/Cell/Cell.tsx

## Rules

- Use only token utilities: the Tailwind theme is closed, so bg-red-500 or p-11 do not exist.
- Two fonts only: font-content (Young Serif) for what is being learned, font-chrome (Instrument Sans) for the app.
- Type is used through the six roles (label, body, title, reading, headline, display), never a size number.
- Contrast is a gate: every text pair 4.5:1, every graphic pair 3:1, in both modes.
- Hit targets are at least 44px.
- Every interactive element has a visible focus ring; disabled never hovers.
